close_reason: Performance optimization deferred to v0.2. Not a correctness issue.
description: When multiple anchors share a DN (key rollover scenario), chain_walk is called once per candidate anchor. Each call re-encodes every cert's TBSCertificate from scratch: N encode_to_slice calls per anchor attempt. For A anchors and N-length chain, total TBS encodings = A*N. In a typical browser trust store with ~130 roots, even 1% name-collision rate means a long chain gets 1-2 extra full encodings — negligible. However, if anchor list is large and name-collision is common (e.g., testing harness with many anchors), this degrades to O(A*N*encode_cost). The fix (cache TBS DER per cert before the anchor loop) would be a non-trivial restructuring since chain_walk owns the buffer. Low actual impact, worth tracking.
title: chain_walk re-encodes TBS N times per anchor attempt
